keyVerseText: And on the morrow when he departed, he took out two pence, and gave them to the host, and said unto him, Take care of him; and whatsoever thou spendest more, when I come again , I will repay thee.
rootMeaning: The Greek verb ἐπανέρχομαι (epanérchomai) is formed from the preposition ἐπί (epi), meaning 'upon' or 'over,' combined with ἀνέρχομαι (anerchomai), meaning 'to go up' or 'to come.' This etymology conveys a literal sense of 'coming back up' or 'returning' to a previous place or point. Beyond the simple English gloss 'return,' the root sense includes the idea of approaching again with purpose or intent, sometimes with a nuance of ascending or revisiting a former state or position.
usageInScripture: The verb ἐπανέρχομαι appears sparingly in the New Testament, with only two recorded occurrences. Its primary translation is 'come again' or 'was returned,' indicating a consistent use to denote a physical or metaphorical return. This limited but focused usage highlights its role in describing deliberate returns, whether to a location or a prior subject in discourse, underscoring both literal and figurative senses of coming back.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding ἐπανέρχομαι enriches our grasp of biblical themes of return and restoration, which are central to the Christian faith. The concept of 'coming again' resonates deeply with the hope of Christ's return and the believer's journey back to God. It captures not only physical movement but also spiritual recapitulation and renewal, emphasizing God's faithfulness in returning to His people and the believer's continual turning back to Him. This word thus embodies the dynamic of repentance, restoration, and the eschatological promise of Christ's second coming.
keyVerseReflection: In Luke 10:35, the phrase 'when I come again' uses ἐπανέρχομαι to express a future, intentional return. The Samaritan’s promise to repay any excess expenses upon his return underscores a commitment to restoration and accountability. The word highlights the certainty and purposefulness of this return, which can also point readers toward the assured return of Christ, who will come again to fulfill His promises and bring ultimate restoration.
